question:
(i) Using Gauss’s law, obtain the expression for electric field outside a uniformly charged thin spherical shell.
(ii) State the value of electric field inside the shell and explain the reason.

options.B:
(i) For $r>R$, $E=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}$
(ii) Inside the shell, the field is maximum
options.C:
(i) For $r>R$, $E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{R^2}$ for every $r$
(ii) Inside the shell, the field varies as $\frac{1}{r^2}$
options.D:
(i) For $r>R$, $E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}$
(ii) Inside, $E=0$ because a Gaussian surface inside encloses no charge
